reviewCadence: At every session, cookie, JWT middleware, refresh-token, login, device fingerprint, request-header, risk-scoring, or step-up policy change.

requirements.name: Capture session establishment context
requirements.owasp: Store IP address, User-Agent, Accept-Language, Date-adjacent request context, Accept, Accept-Encoding, Sec-Fetch, and client hints when creating a session.

controls.name: Server-side session request profile and client hints
controls.description: Request context negotiates Client Hints and verifies client IP and origin headers during authentication.

requirements.name: Persist detection attributes safely
requirements.owasp: Session attributes must be stored server-side so stolen cookies can be compared against the expected session environment.

controls.name: PostgreSQL-backed session storage
controls.description: PostgreSQL stores hashed session tokens with strict expiration and principal mapping.

requirements.name: Detect significant environment changes
requirements.owasp: Compare current request context against the saved session context without relying on exact one-field equality alone.

controls.name: Trust and risk assessment
controls.description: Trust-Risk domain evaluates anomalies, network changes, and suspicious patterns.

requirements.name: Validate every authenticated request
requirements.owasp: Cookie theft detection should run in middleware or at protected endpoint boundaries, with tuning for sensitive paths.

controls.name: JWT session and claims validation
controls.description: Token service decodes and validates claims including subject, issuer, audience, and expiration.

requirements.name: Force reauthentication on high suspicion
requirements.owasp: When hijacking is suspected, invalidate the user's session and require reauthentication for reliable protection.

controls.name: Suspicious-session reauthentication error
controls.description: High suspicion returns an explicit reauthentication-required application error requiring step-up or re-auth.

requirements.name: Record telemetry for investigation
requirements.owasp: Cookie theft detection has false positives and false negatives, so decisions must be auditable and tunable.

controls.name: Risk and audit event trail
controls.description: Suspicious events and authentication decisions are recorded in transactional audit logs.

requirements.name: Harden bearer cookies and browser isolation
requirements.owasp: Cookie theft mitigation complements secure cookie attributes; stolen bearer cookies should be harder to obtain and replay.

controls.name: Clear-Site-Data and browser isolation headers
controls.description: Security headers enforce Clear-Site-Data on logout, frame-ancestors none CSP, and Strict-Transport-Security.

requirements.name: Prevent regressions
requirements.owasp: Cookie theft controls must stay enforced as session and authentication code evolves.

controls.name: Cookie theft mitigation gate
controls.description: The repository check path validates OWASP evidence, session persistence, security headers, reauthentication contracts, and verification scripts.
